title: Sidney Bechet and Mike McKenzie's Paris shoot-out
summary: Bullard told Butler that Bechet and McKenzie argued about a chord in a recording studio and shot at each other in the street, and Bechet went to prison for a year with white hair.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition

blocks.x: -- 65 Second Avenue, the home of Jacques Butler, February 6th, Stanley Crouch interviewing, and we are going to resume Gene Bullard and how he descended Sidney Bechet.

Well, the case was Mike McKenzie, Gene Bullard, come up to de les Tribune, the same region, which was Paris. I think this was around 1924 or something like that. See, this is Gene Bullard who was telling me about this thing. Sidney Bechet and Mike McKenzie were making records. So some change there that Mike McKenzie says, excuse me, but I think that's the wrong chord there. Bechet says, don't worry about it now, Bechet don't make no better chords. But he said, "But, see, it's a C 7 and you made it C-diminished" "Bechet don't make no bad chords, Mike." He says, but that chord you made is more beautiful, the notes is more beautiful. Bechet said, "I told you, Bechet don't make no bad chords," and pulled out a 45 and put it in Mike McKenzie's stomach. McKenzie says, well, you said you didn't make no bad chords but I'll go home and get my 45 and we'll see about those bad chords. What time, then? "I'll meet you at 7:00 o'clock, shooting on sight. On sight." All right, around about 6:30, 7:00, people are coming off from work, all the musicians are coming from work. Too, people are going to work. At that time

they had horses. So, "here you are," boom, boom, they started shooting, shooting at everything, he's drunk and he's shooting. Shot a couple horses in the leg. There's a man, a piano player from Chicago with me, (inaudible), shot him in the leg, shot a couple people, one lady in the head. Oh, it was awful. Then, after he run out of bullets, went home and went to sleep.
(Unintelligible) police got Bechet and Mike McKenzie. Well, Mike McKenzie had that baroness so it seemed like automatically he was released on bond or whatever it was, for his release.

Yeah, he had a baroness, yeah. So Bechet, he didn't have nobody. So Bechet immediately toured -- called the Sante under the Seine (PHONETIC) and he stayed there one year until his case came up. Bechet's hair turned white.
